excerpt: Poonamallee still has open plots, and the risk on them is in the paperwork more than the construction. Here is how we check the layout first, then build on bare ground.
content:
An open plot is not a ready plot

Poonamallee still has open land. Plots here are often bought by families who want room to build, sometimes years before they start. The metro line to Poonamallee and the highway towards Bengaluru have brought more attention to the area, and more layouts to choose from.

Open ground is easier to build on than a crowded street. But the risk on an open plot is not in the construction. It is in the papers. A house on a plot in an unapproved layout can struggle to get a building permit, a bank loan and, later, a buyer.

So as builders in Poonamallee, our team checks the layout before we talk about design.

Checking the layout: what we look at

Poonamallee is inside the Chennai Metropolitan Area. Depending on where the plot falls, the building permit comes from the local body, with CMDA for larger buildings, and the layout itself should carry planning approval. Here is what we check:

  1. Approval number. An approved layout has an approval number from the planning authority. We match it against the approved layout plan, not the promoter's brochure.
  2. Your plot on that plan. The plot number, size and shape should appear on the approved plan exactly as in your sale deed.
  3. Not reserved land. Approved layouts set aside land for roads and open space. Plots carved out of that reserved land are sometimes sold anyway. They cannot be built on.
  4. Roads handed over. In an approved layout, the roads and open space are normally handed to the local body. That is what gets roads maintained and streetlights connected.
  5. Regularisation, if unapproved. If the layout was never approved, ask whether your specific plot was regularised, and get a copy of the order.
  6. Title and patta. Patta subdivided into the seller's name, an encumbrance certificate covering a long enough period, and a clean chain of sale deeds.
  7. Land use. Former farmland should show residential use in the planning records before you build on it.

Our guide on verifying approved plots in Chennai goes through these checks in more detail, and the encumbrance certificate guide explains how to read one.

Building on bare ground

Once the papers are clear, an open plot is a straightforward site. A few things work differently from building on an older street.

  • No neighbours to compare with. On a fresh layout there may be no houses nearby to show how deep foundations needed to go. The soil test is the only reliable guide.
  • Ground level. Some plots in new layouts sit lower than the road that will eventually be laid, or on land that was once farmed. Where the layout plan shows the road level, we set the plinth against that future level, not today's mud track.
  • Water and power. A borewell and a temporary electricity connection usually come first. Check what water supply the local body provides to the layout before you size the sump.
  • Access in the rains. If the layout roads are still unpaved, a loaded lorry can get stuck after heavy rain. We plan the foundation work and bulk deliveries with the monsoon in mind.
  • Site security. An isolated plot needs a fence or compound wall early, and a lockable store for cement and steel.

Funding the build

Many families here bought the plot first and are now building with a home loan. Banks release a construction loan in stages, after their engineer or valuer has seen the work. They also look closely at the layout approval and the building permit, which is one more reason the checks above come first.

Our stage-wise payments line up with how banks disburse. Each stage has a clear description, so the bank's inspection and our invoice describe the same piece of work. Our page on home construction loan disbursement explains how the tranches usually work.

What to bring to the first meeting

  • The sale deed and any earlier deeds for the plot
  • Patta and the encumbrance certificate
  • The layout approval details or regularisation order
  • A copy of the layout sketch showing your plot
  • Any loan sanction letter, if you already have one

What it costs

Our package rates are per sq ft of built-up area: Basic ₹2,199, Standard ₹2,399, Premium ₹2,699 and Ultra Luxury ₹3,199.

A 1,000 sq ft single-storey house at Basic comes to about ₹22 lakh (1,000 × ₹2,199). A 1,600 sq ft two-storey house at Premium is about ₹43.2 lakh (1,600 × ₹2,699).

Approvals, the soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are extra. On a new layout, ask what the quote covers for the borewell and the temporary power connection. We list these as separate lines where they apply, so nothing appears for the first time halfway through the build.

How we handle a Poonamallee build

  1. Site visit to see the plot, the layout roads, and how the site drains.
  2. Plot and document check: layout approval or regularisation, patta, encumbrance certificate and land use, before any design work.
  3. Soil test and design, with the plinth set against the road level the layout plan shows.
  4. Approval from the local body, or CMDA where the building's size requires it.
  5. Stage-wise construction with a daily progress report, useful when you live elsewhere and visit only at weekends.
  6. Stage-wise payments that match the stages your bank inspects.

Send us the layout before you sign

If you are about to buy, or already own, a plot in Poonamallee, send us the layout approval details, the sale deed and the patta. Our team will check them, visit the plot and tell you what can be built there. Of all the builders in Poonamallee you speak to, choose one who asks for these papers before quoting a rate.
faqTitle: Building in Poonamallee: questions owners ask

faqs.question: How do I check whether a Poonamallee layout is approved?
faqs.answer: Ask the seller for the layout approval number and a copy of the approved layout plan. Check that your plot number, size and shape appear on it as in your sale deed, and that the plot is not carved out of land reserved for roads or open space. Confirm the approval with the authority that issued it.

faqs.question: Which authority approves house plans in Poonamallee?
faqs.answer: For a typical individual house, the building permit comes from the local body for your plot, with CMDA handling larger buildings. Which local body applies depends on where the plot sits, so we confirm it during the document check.

faqs.question: Can I build on a plot in an unapproved layout?
faqs.answer: Only with difficulty unless the plot has been regularised. Without approval or regularisation, building permits and home loans are hard to get. If the layout was not approved, ask for the regularisation order for your specific plot before you pay anything.

faqs.question: Do I need a soil test on a new layout plot?
faqs.answer: Yes. On a fresh layout there are often no nearby houses to show how deep foundations should go, and some plots were farmland or low ground. The soil test tells our engineer what the foundation needs.

faqs.question: Will a bank give a construction loan for my Poonamallee plot?
faqs.answer: Banks generally lend for construction on plots with clear title, an approved or regularised layout and a building permit, and they release funds in stages after inspection. Our stage-wise payments are set out to match those stages.

faqs.question: What does a 1,000 sq ft house cost to build in Poonamallee?
faqs.answer: About ₹22 lakh at our Basic package (₹2,199 per sq ft). Approvals, soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are extra, and on a new layout the borewell and temporary power connection are listed separately where they apply.
